$HNRG Q3 2026 earnings: Hallador signs record power contracts, but takes on costly debt

Hallador Energy, an Indiana coal and power producer, bounced back from a summer plant outage and locked in its highest electricity prices ever, while taking on expensive debt to build a second power plant. Quarterly sales rose 28% from the second quarter to $130 million as power generation jumped, narrowing the net loss to $4.5 million. In October, chief executive Brent Bilsland signed a multi-year power deal above $80 per megawatt-hour that lifted the total segment backlog to $3.0 billion.

• Total revenue: $𝟏𝟑𝟎.𝟑𝐌 (-11% from a year ago, +28% from last quarter)
• Contracted power backlog: $𝟐.𝟐𝟐𝐁 (+38% from last quarter on October deal)
• Total debt: $𝟓𝟓𝟏.𝟗𝐌 (up from $45.0M after $600M bridge loan)
• Turtle Creek investment decision: 𝐁𝐞𝐟𝐨𝐫𝐞 𝐲𝐞𝐚𝐫-𝐞𝐧𝐝 (pushed back from September 2026)

⚖️ 𝐕𝐞𝐫𝐝𝐢𝐜𝐭: ⚪ Neutral

The story is unchanged because solving the gas turbine funding crunch came with a steep financing bill that offsets the new power contract. Securing a $600 million bridge loan allowed Hallador to take ownership of its turbines in the Philippines and put $265 million into escrow without selling new shares today. The bad news: the loan requires a minimum repayment of 1.35 times the funded amount even on a refinancing—at least $743 million on the $550 million draw by our math—and outside power purchases hit $11 million despite the planned outage ending.

The question now is whether signing long-term customers for the Turtle Creek gas plant in early 2027 lets Hallador replace the bridge loan and cover the rest of the $800 million budget without issuing heavy equity. If buyers sign up at high capacity rates, project lenders could fund the gap; if talks drag on, paid-in-kind interest and the 1.35 times payoff floor will squeeze shareholders. The final investment decision before year-end and early 2027 contract announcements will settle it.

Full article with charts - link in bio

🐂 𝐁𝐮𝐥𝐥 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐞

🟢🟢 𝐎𝐜𝐭𝐨𝐛𝐞𝐫 𝐃𝐞𝐚𝐥 𝐏𝐮𝐬𝐡𝐞𝐬 𝐏𝐨𝐰𝐞𝐫 𝐁𝐚𝐜𝐤𝐥𝐨𝐠 𝐭𝐨 $𝟐.𝟐 𝐁𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧
Hallador produces electricity at its Merom coal plant in Indiana and sells both energy and accredited capacity, which is a commitment to have power ready when the grid needs it. In October, the Indiana power producer signed its third major multi-year supply deal of 2026, locking in prices starting in 2029.

• Combined price on the October deal: over $80 per megawatt-hour, the highest in the company's history
• Total contracted power backlog: $2.22 billion, up 38% ($616 million) from last quarter by our math
• Average contracted capacity and energy price: rises from $46.07 per megawatt-hour in 2026 to $75.35 in 2031–2035

This matters because the October contract pairs high-grade energy prices with the capacity deals signed earlier this year. Earlier, the company kept its energy beyond 2028 open to wait for better prices. Getting over $80 per megawatt-hour proves buyers will pay a premium for guaranteed power late in the decade.

What to watch: contracted energy volumes for 2029 and 2030 in the fourth-quarter report. Adding more volume near $50 per megawatt-hour would show the October pricing applies across the rest of the plant's open output.

🟢 𝐆𝐫𝐢𝐝 𝐒𝐭𝐮𝐝𝐲 𝐂𝐨𝐦𝐩𝐥𝐞𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐀𝐝𝐯𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞𝐬 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐆𝐚𝐬 𝐏𝐥𝐚𝐧𝐭
Turtle Creek is Hallador's planned 460-megawatt natural gas power plant next to its existing Indiana station. "MISO notified us that the interconnection study, which ran through MISO’s Expedited Resource Addition Study program, is complete," chief executive Brent Bilsland said, referring to the regional grid operator's fast-track review.

In October, the power producer also took legal ownership of unused gas turbines bought for $350 million in the Philippines and put the remaining $265 million purchase price into escrow. Those turbines are now on a ship to the United States for Siemens to inspect, keeping the second half of 2028 start date within reach.

What to watch: the signed grid interconnection agreement and the upgrade cost bill in the fourth-quarter filing. A manageable grid upgrade bill would clear the way for the board's final investment decision before year-end.

🐻 𝐁𝐞𝐚𝐫 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐞

🔴🔴 𝐓𝐡𝐞 $𝟔𝟎𝟎 𝐌𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐁𝐫𝐢𝐝𝐠𝐞 𝐋𝐨𝐚𝐧 𝐂𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐢𝐞𝐬 𝐚 𝟏.𝟑𝟓𝐱 𝐏𝐚𝐲𝐨𝐟𝐟 𝐂𝐨𝐬𝐭
Last quarter, Hallador owed $339 million for its gas turbines with only $84 million in liquidity, creating a risk of default or heavy share sales. Management wants to build the gas project and "build value at each development stage with little to no equity dilution", Bilsland said, while expanding the project makes the business attractive and "broadens the group of investors who can own our shares and finance our company".

This quarter, the power producer closed the funding gap by taking out a $600 million senior secured construction bridge loan, drawing $550 million at closing. That cash paid off old bank debt, triggered a $5.7 million debt extinguishment loss, and put $330 million into restricted cash to cover the turbine escrow.

However, the loan terms in the risk disclosures show a steep price. The facility charges paid-in-kind interest, puts liens on almost all assets, and requires "a minimum return of 1.35 times the funded amount payable on any repayment (including a refinancing)". By our math, repaying or refinancing the $550 million draw will cost at least $742.5 million, an extra $192.5 million on a project budgeted at $800 million.

What to watch: the interest rate and maturity schedule of the $600 million bridge loan in the third-quarter 10-Q filing. Those details will show how fast paid-in-kind interest builds toward the 1.35 times repayment floor.

🔴 𝐎𝐮𝐭𝐬𝐢𝐝𝐞 𝐏𝐨𝐰𝐞𝐫 𝐏𝐮𝐫𝐜𝐡𝐚𝐬𝐞𝐬 𝐒𝐭𝐚𝐲𝐞𝐝 𝐇𝐢𝐠𝐡 𝐀𝐟𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐎𝐮𝐭𝐚𝐠𝐞
When Hallador's coal units break down during hot weather, the utility has to buy replacement electricity on the open market to meet its delivery contracts. In the second quarter, unplanned downtime at Unit 2 pushed purchased power costs up to $8.6 million while Unit 1 sat in a 60-day planned maintenance outage that finished in July.

Power generation jumped 77% from the second quarter to 1.4 million megawatt-hours once Unit 1 returned, cutting maintenance costs by 6.1 percentage points of revenue from a year ago. Yet the cost of purchased power rose again to $11.1 million, or 8.5% of revenue, up 7.1 percentage points from a year ago, while labor rose 4.6 points and overhead rose 2.1 points.

What to watch: unit availability and purchased power expense in the fourth quarter, when no major outage is scheduled. Another quarter above $6 million in outside power purchases would point to ongoing reliability problems on the 1980s coal units.

🔴 𝐍𝐞𝐰 𝐄𝐧𝐞𝐫𝐠𝐲 𝐂𝐨𝐧𝐭𝐫𝐚𝐜𝐭 𝐈𝐧𝐜𝐥𝐮𝐝𝐞𝐬 𝐚 𝟗𝟎-𝐃𝐚𝐲 𝐁𝐮𝐲𝐞𝐫 𝐂𝐮𝐭𝐨𝐮𝐭
The headline $3.0 billion segment backlog includes $421.5 million of energy sales between 2029 and 2035 from the new October contract. Unlike standard fixed-volume deals, the footnote explains that those figures are management estimates derived from forward power curves.

The contract covers a base load of 200 megawatts, but it is unit-contingent—meaning required volumes drop if a Merom generating unit is offline—and it "permits the counterparty to reduce the base quantity to zero for a maximum of 90 days per year". Because the buyer can turn off deliveries for a quarter of the year when market prices are low, realized sales could fall well below the backlog table.

What to watch: whether future supply contracts for Merom and Turtle Creek give buyers similar 90-day volume options. Relying on flexible volume clauses would make post-2028 cash flows less predictable than fixed capacity payments.

🔴 𝐑𝐢𝐬𝐤𝐬 𝐓𝐡𝐢𝐬 𝐐𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐃𝐢𝐝𝐧'𝐭 𝐀𝐧𝐬𝐰𝐞𝐫
Three standing risks in the business received no resolution in the third-quarter earnings release.

• Indiana regulator approval: the 12-year capacity contract over $1 billion still awaits Indiana Utility Regulatory Commission sign-off, which was targeted on or before November 15, 2026.
• Gas plant customer contracts: Turtle Creek still has no signed buyer agreements, with management now targeting deals with investment-grade customers in early 2027.
• Coal plant rules and outside buyers: third-party coal sales fell 30% from a year ago, and the release gives no update on post-2030 environmental compliance costs at Merom.

👓 𝐎𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐓𝐡𝐞𝐦𝐞𝐬

𝐏𝐨𝐰𝐞𝐫 𝐁𝐮𝐲𝐞𝐫𝐬 𝐏𝐚𝐲 𝐓𝐫𝐢𝐩𝐥𝐞 𝐭𝐨 𝐋𝐨𝐜𝐤 𝐈𝐧 𝐒𝐮𝐩𝐩𝐥𝐲 𝐀𝐟𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟖
Across the Midcontinent grid, utilities and data centers face a shortage of power plants that can run on demand rather than only when the wind blows or the sun shines. That scarcity is visible in Hallador's contracted capacity prices, which jump from $244 per megawatt-day in 2026 to $478 in 2029 and $502 in 2030.

— • — • —

💲 𝐎𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐊𝐏𝐈𝐬

𝐂𝐨𝐧𝐭𝐫𝐚𝐜𝐭 𝐥𝐢𝐚𝐛𝐢𝐥𝐢𝐭𝐢𝐞𝐬 / 𝐝𝐞𝐟𝐞𝐫𝐫𝐞𝐝 𝐫𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐧𝐮𝐞 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): $𝟏𝟏𝟑.𝟕 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇘ decelerating
Contract liabilities—cash customers paid upfront in 2024 and 2025 for electricity to be delivered later—fell 23.7% from $149.1 million at the end of 2025, by our math. As Hallador delivers this low-priced power without cash coming in, nine-month operating cash flow was negative $25.1 million. Management says these legacy prepaid deals expire in the second quarter of 2027.

𝐓𝐡𝐢𝐫𝐝-𝐩𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐲 𝐜𝐨𝐚𝐥 𝐫𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐧𝐮𝐞 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): $𝟑𝟔.𝟏 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇘ decelerating
Sales of coal from Sunrise Coal to outside buyers dropped 29.5% from a year ago and 11.0% from the second quarter. Lower outside coal revenue caused the 11.1% drop in total quarterly company sales, while electric revenue held steady from a year ago at $92.8 million.

𝐅𝐫𝐞𝐞 𝐜𝐚𝐬𝐡 𝐟𝐥𝐨𝐰 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): -$𝟕𝟖.𝟗 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇘ decelerating
By our math, cash burn widened from negative $50.2 million in the second quarter and positive $3.7 million a year ago. Hallador used $21.8 million in operating cash flow while spending $57.1 million on capital projects for the gas turbines and July coal plant upgrades.

— • — • —

🔮 𝐆𝐮𝐢𝐝𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞

𝐓𝐮𝐫𝐭𝐥𝐞 𝐂𝐫𝐞𝐞𝐤 𝐅𝐢𝐧𝐚𝐥 𝐈𝐧𝐯𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭 𝐃𝐞𝐜𝐢𝐬𝐢𝐨𝐧: 𝐁𝐞𝐟𝐨𝐫𝐞 𝐲𝐞𝐚𝐫-𝐞𝐧𝐝 𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟔  ⇘ decelerating
🠇 cut from September 2026
Pushed back by up to three months. The power producer previously targeted September 2026 for both the board's final investment decision and the signed grid connection contract. Although the grid operator finished its study, the final grid contract, construction agreement, and remaining equipment orders are still being completed.

𝐓𝐮𝐫𝐭𝐥𝐞 𝐂𝐫𝐞𝐞𝐤 𝐂𝐨𝐦𝐦𝐞𝐫𝐜𝐢𝐚𝐥 𝐎𝐩𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐃𝐚𝐭𝐞: 𝐒𝐞𝐜𝐨𝐧𝐝 𝐡𝐚𝐥𝐟 𝐨𝐟 𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟖  ⇒ stable
🠆 unchanged from Second half of 2028
Unchanged. The company still plans to start running the 460-megawatt gas plant in the second half of 2028, despite the one-month delay in shipping the turbines from the Philippines and the later investment decision. Hitting this date is required under the new $600 million credit agreement to avoid an event of default.

𝐓𝐮𝐫𝐭𝐥𝐞 𝐂𝐫𝐞𝐞𝐤 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐣𝐞𝐜𝐭 𝐂𝐨𝐬𝐭 & 𝐕𝐚𝐥𝐮𝐞 𝐓𝐚𝐫𝐠𝐞𝐭: $𝟖𝟎𝟎𝐌 𝐢𝐧𝐯𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭 / ~$𝟏.𝟔𝐁 𝐭𝐚𝐫𝐠𝐞𝐭 𝐯𝐚𝐥𝐮𝐞  ⇗ accelerating
🠆 unchanged from Below $800 million
Unchanged on cost, with a new value target added. "Our goal at Turtle Creek is to seek to roughly double an $800 million investment into $1.6 billion of value over the next 24 months," chief executive Brent Bilsland said. Management added that the $600 million bridge loan and a planned $75 million credit line leave more capital still to be raised.

— • — • —

❓ 𝐊𝐞𝐲 𝐐𝐮𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬

𝐖𝐡𝐞𝐧 𝐜𝐚𝐧 𝐇𝐚𝐥𝐥𝐚𝐝𝐨𝐫 𝐫𝐞𝐟𝐢𝐧𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝟏.𝟑𝟓𝐱 𝐛𝐫𝐢𝐝𝐠𝐞 𝐥𝐨𝐚𝐧 𝐰𝐢𝐭𝐡𝐨𝐮𝐭 𝐩𝐞𝐧𝐚𝐥𝐭𝐲?
The $600 million bridge loan requires a minimum repayment of 1.35 times the funded amount ($742.5 million on the $550 million draw) even on a refinancing. Investors need to know the interest rate and whether signing customer contracts lowers that payoff multiple.

𝐖𝐡𝐲 𝐝𝐢𝐝 𝐨𝐮𝐭𝐬𝐢𝐝𝐞 𝐩𝐨𝐰𝐞𝐫 𝐩𝐮𝐫𝐜𝐡𝐚𝐬𝐞𝐬 𝐫𝐞𝐚𝐜𝐡 $𝟏𝟏.𝟏 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐢𝐧 𝐐𝟑?

$MARA Q3 2026 earnings: MARA pays off its Bitcoin loans, but lease targets slip

MARA, a Bitcoin miner expanding into artificial intelligence data centers, saw mining revenue drop while paper gains lifted net profit. Revenue fell 35% to $164 million as lower Bitcoin prices outweighed a 5% rise in coins mined. Reported profit reached $632 million only because of an $885 million accounting gain on its coin stash. After the quarter ended, the finance chief sold 13,597 Bitcoin to pay off $750 million of debt.

• Revenue: $𝟏𝟔𝟒.𝟐𝐌 (-35% from a year ago)
• Operating loss, excluding crypto paper swings: -$𝟐𝟐𝟔𝐌 (-$182M a year ago, by our math)
• Bitcoin holdings after October sales: 𝟐𝟎,𝟒𝟏𝟓 𝐁𝐓𝐂 (35,577 BTC at the end of Q2, by our math)
• Data center lease outlook: 𝐂𝐮𝐭 (2 leases targeted for 2026 could slip into 2027)

⚖️ 𝐕𝐞𝐫𝐝𝐢𝐜𝐭: ⚪ Neutral

The story is unchanged because solving the debt risk came with another delay in signing data center tenants. Paying off the $750 million loan freed 17,477 pledged coins and removed the threat of collateral calls. The bad news: the chief executive warned that its goal of signing two data center leases this year could slip into 2027, leaving only a $79 million cloud deal as proof of the new business.

The question now is whether MARA's power sites can attract large data center tenants on financeable terms. Either waiting secures better lease economics as power gets scarcer, or rival operators lock up the best customers first. Signed lease announcements over the next two quarters will settle it.

Full article with charts - link in bio

🐂 𝐁𝐮𝐥𝐥 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐞

🟢🟢 𝐁𝐢𝐭𝐜𝐨𝐢𝐧 𝐒𝐚𝐥𝐞𝐬 𝐂𝐥𝐞𝐚𝐫𝐞𝐝 $𝟕𝟓𝟎 𝐌𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐨𝐟 𝐏𝐥𝐞𝐝𝐠𝐞𝐝 𝐃𝐞𝐛𝐭
MARA, a Bitcoin miner expanding into data centers, borrowed $750 million against its digital coins in August to help buy the Long Ridge power plant. That loan locked up more than half of its Bitcoin stash as collateral and raised the risk of forced top-ups if coin prices fell. After the third quarter ended, the finance chief sold 13,597 Bitcoin at about $81,039 each, raising $1.1 billion in cash.

The company used $750 million of those proceeds to pay off the Bitcoin-backed loans in full. That payment freed 17,477 pledged coins, "leaving less than 5% of our BTC holdings loaned or pledged" according to the chief executive. Selling coins after prices rose from $64,000 created an estimated $170 million net benefit, the finance chief said, though MARA also sold 3.8 million shares in July.

What to watch: how much cash MARA sets aside for its 2027 convertible bond obligations. Bondholders can force the company to buy back those notes next year, so keeping cash on hand avoids new borrowing.

🟢 𝐏𝐨𝐰𝐞𝐫 𝐏𝐨𝐫𝐭𝐟𝐨𝐥𝐢𝐨 𝐂𝐥𝐞𝐚𝐫𝐞𝐝 𝐊𝐞𝐲 𝐇𝐮𝐫𝐝𝐥𝐞 𝐚𝐭 𝐋𝐨𝐧𝐠 𝐑𝐢𝐝𝐠𝐞
MARA wants to turn its 1.9 gigawatts of power capacity into a 4.8-gigawatt platform for artificial intelligence data centers. After the quarter ended, federal energy regulators approved its purchase of Long Ridge, an Ohio natural gas plant with 485 megawatts of power capacity. The finance chief expects the deal to close by year-end and bring immediate cash flow, "with roughly 70% of its output under long-term contracts".

Separately, Exaion, MARA's majority-owned cloud computing unit in Europe, signed a four-year, $79 million contract with its first US customer. The buyer agreed to pay for the graphics-chip capacity whether it uses the machines or not, which the chief executive called "an early proof point" for the business. However, Exaion's broader $3 billion pipeline consists of "indications of demand and are not yet contracted or committed".

What to watch: the closing statement for Long Ridge in the fourth-quarter report. It will show how much plant debt joins the balance sheet and how much power profit the plant generates.

🐻 𝐁𝐞𝐚𝐫 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐞

🔴🔴 𝐃𝐚𝐭𝐚 𝐂𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐋𝐞𝐚𝐬𝐞 𝐓𝐚𝐫𝐠𝐞𝐭 𝐂𝐨𝐮𝐥𝐝 𝐒𝐥𝐢𝐩 𝐈𝐧𝐭𝐨 𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟕
For three quarters, MARA has promised to sign large data center tenants to long-term leases alongside its partner Starwood. In the first quarter it targeted at least one lease by the end of 2026, and in the second quarter it raised that goal to two. Management frames the delay as discipline, with the chief executive writing that "waiting has improved the terms available to us".

Yet the quarter ended with zero signed data center leases, and management softened its timeline. "While we are targeting signing two leases before year-end, market conditions are fluid and that timing could slip into next year," the chief executive wrote. Meanwhile, MARA posted a $100 million letter of credit after quarter-end for grid studies at its 2-gigawatt Texas site, committing capital before any tenant signs.

What to watch: any signed lease announcement with a named data center tenant before the fourth-quarter report. Another quarter without a contract would leave MARA relying entirely on Bitcoin and gas power sales.

🔴🔴 𝐀𝐜𝐜𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐆𝐚𝐢𝐧𝐬 𝐌𝐚𝐬𝐤𝐞𝐝 𝐚 𝐒𝐭𝐞𝐞𝐩 𝐌𝐢𝐧𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐋𝐨𝐬𝐬
MARA reported $632.1 million in net income and $857.7 million in Adjusted EBITDA, a profit measure that excludes interest, taxes, depreciation, and stock pay. Both numbers look high only because accounting rules include an $885.3 million paper gain from higher Bitcoin prices during the quarter. Revenue fell 35% to $164.2 million because the average price of Bitcoin mined dropped 37% from a year ago.

• Operating loss excluding crypto and derivative paper swings: $226.4 million by our math, wider than $182.2 million a year ago
• Power and hosting costs: 72.8% of revenue, up 25.8 percentage points from a year ago by our math
• Depreciation and overhead (G&A): 91.9% and 46.2% of revenue, up 25.6 and 12.4 percentage points by our math
• Purchased energy cost per Bitcoin at owned sites: $39,674, up 1.1% from a year ago

By our math, stripping out the $885.3 million crypto paper gain leaves Adjusted EBITDA at negative $27.7 million. Unit energy costs crept up, "primarily driven by higher power costs and global network difficulty outpacing our hashrate growth" according to the finance chief, and third-party hosting contracts worth $71.5 million a quarter do not begin expiring until late 2027.

What to watch: purchased energy cost per Bitcoin in the fourth quarter. If network competition keeps rising faster than MARA's computing capacity, mining margins will stay compressed unless coin prices climb.

🔴 𝐑𝐢𝐬𝐤𝐬 𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐬 𝐪𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐝𝐢𝐝𝐧'𝐭 𝐚𝐧𝐬𝐰𝐞𝐫
Several standing financial, cost, and legal risks received no detailed update in the shareholder letter.

• Overhead cost trend: G&A excluding stock pay and deal costs was $45.4 million by our math, up from $42.4 million last quarter, and the full 10-Q filing will show whether Exaion drove the increase.
• 2027 convertible bond puts: management noted it is monitoring bondholder repayment rights next year, but the 10-Q debt footnotes will show the exact cash liability remaining.
• Legal appeals and international revenue goal: the release did not mention the pending legal appeals or the older goal of getting half of revenue outside the US by 2028.

👓 𝐎𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐓𝐡𝐞𝐦𝐞𝐬

𝐁𝐨𝐚𝐫𝐝 𝐀𝐩𝐩𝐫𝐨𝐯𝐞𝐝 𝐚 $𝟓𝟎𝟎 𝐌𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐒𝐡𝐚𝐫𝐞 𝐁𝐮𝐲𝐛𝐚𝐜𝐤
After the quarter ended, MARA's board approved a programme to buy back up to $500 million of its common stock. Management said the authorization gives it another way to allocate capital alongside debt reduction and data center spending, though it does not obligate the company to buy any specific amount. The digital infrastructure group has not repurchased any shares yet and still has $1.5 billion left on its share-sale programme.

𝐂𝐚𝐮𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐮𝐬 𝐀𝐈 𝐅𝐢𝐧𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐂𝐥𝐢𝐦𝐚𝐭𝐞 𝐒𝐥𝐨𝐰𝐬 𝐈𝐧𝐝𝐮𝐬𝐭𝐫𝐲 𝐃𝐞𝐚𝐥𝐬
The chief executive noted that investors and lenders have grown more cautious toward artificial intelligence infrastructure because of local community opposition, higher borrowing costs, and complex tenant credit structures. While compute demand remains strong, lenders and customers now demand permitted power and guaranteed delivery schedules before committing capital. MARA said this stricter financing environment slows down industry deal-making but favors operators that already control energized land.

— • — • —

💲 𝐎𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐊𝐏𝐈𝐬

𝐁𝐢𝐭𝐜𝐨𝐢𝐧 𝐡𝐨𝐥𝐝𝐢𝐧𝐠𝐬 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): 𝟑𝟒,𝟎𝟏𝟐 𝐁𝐓𝐂  ⇘ decelerating
Total Bitcoin held fell by 1,565 coins from last quarter and by 18,838 coins from a year ago. MARA mined 2,247 coins during the quarter but sold 3,891 coins at an average price of $75,300. After quarter-end, the company sold another 13,597 coins to pay off debt, leaving about 20,415 coins by our math.

𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐡 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐜𝐚𝐬𝐡 𝐞𝐪𝐮𝐢𝐯𝐚𝐥𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐬 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): $𝟗𝟒𝟔.𝟓 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇗ accelerating
Unrestricted cash more than doubled from $421.3 million last quarter and rose 73% from $547.1 million at the end of 2025. The increase came from borrowing against Bitcoin, selling mined coins, and issuing 3.8 million shares in July. Combined cash and Bitcoin totaled $3.8 billion at quarter-end, up from $2.5 billion in the second quarter.

𝐃𝐢𝐥𝐮𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐬𝐡𝐚𝐫𝐞 𝐜𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐭 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): 𝟒𝟗𝟔.𝟒 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇗ accelerating
The diluted share count rose 5.6% from 470.1 million a year ago, while basic shares grew 3.7% to 385.7 million. Because MARA posted a GAAP profit this quarter, potential shares from convertible bonds were counted in the diluted total. The company also resumed selling stock in July, issuing 3.8 million shares after two quarters of zero sales.

— • — • —

🔮 𝐆𝐮𝐢𝐝𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞

𝐂𝐨𝐦𝐦𝐞𝐫𝐜𝐢𝐚𝐥 𝐃𝐚𝐭𝐚 𝐂𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐋𝐞𝐚𝐬𝐞𝐬 (𝐘𝐄 𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟔): 𝟐 𝐥𝐞𝐚𝐬𝐞𝐬 𝐭𝐚𝐫𝐠𝐞𝐭𝐞𝐝 (𝐜𝐨𝐮𝐥𝐝 𝐬𝐥𝐢𝐩 𝐭𝐨 𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟕)  ⇘ decelerating
🠇 cut from At least 1 to 2 leases before year-end
Cut. The chief executive still targets signing two tenant leases before year-end, but warned that fluid market conditions could push the signings into 2027. In the first quarter management targeted one or more leases this year, and in the second quarter it aimed for at least two without any caveat. Zero data center leases have been signed across the past three quarters.

𝐋𝐨𝐧𝐠 𝐑𝐢𝐝𝐠𝐞 𝐍𝐚𝐦𝐞𝐩𝐥𝐚𝐭𝐞 𝐂𝐚𝐩𝐚𝐜𝐢𝐭𝐲 (𝟏𝐇 𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟕): 𝟓𝟎𝟓 𝐌𝐖  ⇒ stable
🠇 cut from 505 MW in 2H 2026
Cut. The Ohio natural gas plant is authorized to sell 485 megawatts today and is now expected to reach its full 505-megawatt capacity in the first half of 2027. In the first quarter, management had expected that 20-megawatt expansion to happen in the second half of 2026. The acquisition itself received federal approval and remains on track to close by year-end 2026.

𝐓𝐡𝐢𝐫𝐝-𝐏𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐲 𝐇𝐨𝐬𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐄𝐱𝐩𝐢𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬 (𝐐𝟑 𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟕–𝐐𝟏 𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟖): 𝟐𝟗% 𝐨𝐟 𝐞𝐧𝐞𝐫𝐠𝐲 𝐜𝐚𝐩𝐚𝐜𝐢𝐭𝐲 𝐞𝐱𝐩𝐢𝐫𝐢𝐧𝐠  ⇒ stable
🠆 unchanged from Expiring Q3 2027 to Q1 2028
Unchanged. Management reiterated that its largest third-party hosting contracts, which make up about 29% of total energy capacity, will begin expiring in the third quarter of 2027 and end completely in the first quarter of 2028. Exiting those sites will eliminate third-party hosting expenses, which cost $71.5 million this quarter and $210.7 million over the first nine months of 2026.

— • — • —

❓ 𝐊𝐞𝐲 𝐐𝐮𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬

𝐇𝐨𝐰 𝐦𝐮𝐜𝐡 𝐜𝐚𝐬𝐡 𝐫𝐞𝐦𝐚𝐢𝐧𝐬 𝐚𝐟𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐋𝐨𝐧𝐠 𝐑𝐢𝐝𝐠𝐞 𝐜𝐥𝐨𝐬𝐞𝐬?
MARA raised $1.1 billion from October Bitcoin sales and spent $750 million to pay off crypto-backed loans. Because those loans were originally taken to fund the Long Ridge purchase, investors need to know how much cash the closing itself will consume before year-end.

𝐖𝐡𝐲 𝐝𝐢𝐝 𝐌𝐀𝐑𝐀 𝐢𝐬𝐬𝐮𝐞 𝐬𝐡𝐚𝐫𝐞𝐬 𝐢𝐧 𝐉𝐮𝐥𝐲 𝐛𝐞𝐟𝐨𝐫𝐞 𝐚𝐩𝐩𝐫𝐨𝐯𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐛𝐮𝐲𝐛𝐚𝐜𝐤𝐬?
The company sold 3.8 million shares under its at-the-market stock programme in July after two quarters without dilution, then authorized a $500 million buyback after quarter-end. Management did not give the July sale price or explain what changed its view on issuing equity.

𝐖𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐚𝐫𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐨𝐧𝐞𝐬 𝐟𝐨𝐫 𝐭𝐡𝐞 $𝟏𝟎𝟎 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐓𝐞𝐱𝐚𝐬 𝐝𝐞𝐩𝐨𝐬𝐢𝐭?
After quarter-end, MARA posted a $100 million letter of credit for grid interconnection studies at its 2-gigawatt Matagorda County site. Management has not disclosed when the state grid operator will finish the study or when purchase payments to the seller begin.

𝐖𝐡𝐨 𝐢𝐬 𝐄𝐱𝐚𝐢𝐨𝐧'𝐬 $𝟕𝟗 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐔𝐒 𝐜𝐮𝐬𝐭𝐨𝐦𝐞𝐫?
Exaion signed a four-year, $79 million graphics-chip contract with its first US buyer on take-or-pay terms. Management did not disclose the customer's credit profile, how much capital MARA must spend to buy the chips, or when the revenue starts.

Today's CRISPR trial at AHA was in people with very high triglycerides, so a quick guide to what that means on a lab report.

1. Normal is under 150 mg/dL (1.7 mmol/L). Severe is 500 mg/dL (5.6 mmol/L) or more.
2. Above about 1,000 mg/dL (11.3 mmol/L), the blood is usually full of chylomicrons, the sample can look milky, and the risk of acute pancreatitis rises.
3. A milky sample can throw off other results too. Sodium can read falsely low on some analysers.
4. Most severe cases have a second cause on top of a genetic tendency. Look for uncontrolled diabetes, alcohol, an underactive thyroid, kidney disease, pregnancy, and medicines such as oestrogens, steroids, retinoids and some antipsychotics.
5. At that level the first steps are usually stopping alcohol, getting glucose under control and a very low-fat diet, with drug treatment decided by the treating doctor.

Most high triglyceride results are in the mild to moderate range, where the bigger question is the person's overall heart risk.

One piece most people miss in the Nvidia story:

Who actually controls Nvidia, and what happens next?

Unlike Meta, SpaceX or Alphabet, Nvidia has no founder super-voting share structure.

Jensen Huang owns only around 3–4%.

Vanguard, BlackRock and State Street are among its largest institutional shareholders.

The same asset-management giants that hold major stakes across banking, defence and technology.

But ownership, voting influence and operational control are different things.

Nvidia sits at the intersection of three forces:

FIC: Institutional capital and financial markets.

MIC: US national-security interests and export controls.

TIC: Semiconductor technology, AI infrastructure and the chokepoints of TSMC and ASML.

The Chinese spy story is interesting, but I’m watching something bigger.

Could this become the catalyst for a corporate regime change at Nvidia?

A founder CEO without majority voting control is not immune to pressure from institutional shareholders, the board or the state.

An espionage controversy, export-control investigation or national-security dispute could create the conditions for a leadership change, governance restructuring or even a takeover attempt.

That doesn’t mean any of those outcomes are planned or inevitable.

But it’s where I’ll be looking.

Will institutional shareholders increase pressure?

Will the board’s position change?

Will Washington use national-security powers to demand greater oversight?

Will strategic investors emerge, or will Nvidia’s independence become a political issue?

A takeover of Nvidia would face enormous financial, regulatory and national-security obstacles.

A regime change in leadership or governance could be a very different proposition.

The point is that controlling the CEO and controlling the company are not the same thing.

Intelligence agencies, including Mossad, have historically operated through covert networks and methods designed to preserve plausible deniability.

Meanwhile, North Korea, China, Iran and Russia frequently feature in Western intelligence attribution narratives.

We don’t know the full story behind these allegations yet.

And I assume that what we’re being told is not true.

The real question isn’t simply whether the spy allegations are true.

It’s whether they become a catalyst for shifting power over one of the most strategically important companies in the AI economy.

That’s what I’m watching next.

While this alters cash flow timing, it does not erase total construction costs.
2) Management guides for positive free cash flow in 2H FY2028, whereas Goldman Sachs models full-year FCF inflection in FY2029 at $2.79 billion against operating cash flow of $98.2 billion. The variance between semi-annual and annual definitions warrants ongoing monitoring of deployment milestones and collections.
3) The 7 GW targeted for energization by May 2028 is fully contracted and under construction. Of the 10 GW FY2028 pipeline, five flagship campuses account for less than half, with the balance distributed across 38 multinational sites; air-quality permitting in New Mexico remains an active operational risk. "Amid compute supply shortages, suppliers are willing to co-fund builds in exchange for long-term component share, while customers secure direct hardware discounts—enabling Oracle to lock in bookings while protecting unit margins." CoreWeave: Balance-sheet pressures pose a more direct threat to expansion than equity volatility; upcoming earnings must address how backlog converts into bankable cash flow.
1) Market reports indicate that select bond yields rose above 16%, while 5-year credit default swap (CDS) spreads widened past 1,240 bps, up roughly 50% over the trailing month. CDS spreads price default risk; wider spreads imply steeper costs for credit protection and incremental capital rather than an active default.
2) The company is scheduled to report earnings after the market close on Tuesday, November 10, 2026. Beyond topline growth, customer cash receipts, hardware capex pacing, and debt structures will determine the sustainability of its expansion. Even if underlying GPU demand holds firm, prohibitive financing rates compress unit project economics.
3) Shares were down 42.19% over the 20 trading sessions ending November 9, 2026. While credit strains and equity declines are correlated, the selloff should not be read as evidence of customer cancellations until confirmed by operational updates. Nebius: Geographic footprint diversifies regulatory exposure away from Texas-concentrated peers, but financing and operational delivery still require site-by-site evaluation.
1) Rosenblatt noted that Nebius's largest quantified U.S. expansion pipeline is located in Missouri, Pennsylvania, and South Carolina, where policy headwinds are comparatively muted relative to planned capacity. This assessment applies to its specific footprint rather than the broader data center permitting landscape.
2) Over the trailing 20 and 60 trading days through November 9, 2026, the stock fell 38.36% and 53.37%, respectively, reflecting steep market discounts on long-dated capacity conversion.
3) Geographic diversification mitigates single-state utility bottlenecks, but land, power hookups, and customer commitments must still align. Whether reduced regulatory friction translates into an operating advantage depends on execution rather than site selection lists alone. "Its largest quantified U.S. expansion pipeline is situated across Missouri, Pennsylvania, and South Carolina." IREN: Operating assets demonstrate strong revenue momentum, but pipeline capacity cannot be recognized ahead of energization.
1) In its latest quarterly filing, AI cloud revenue surged 182% quarter-over-quarter to roughly $200 million, accounting for nearly 90% of total revenue. Management noted that older H100 GPUs were renewed under multi-year contracts at 100% higher rates, with select customer prepayments covering up to 90% of hardware procurement costs. Robust renewal pricing confirms that economic lifespans for previous-generation silicon remain intact.
2) IREN stated it has secured all required permits for its current phase, with the energization of Childress and ongoing Horizon 1 deliveries to Microsoft underpinning near-term cash flow.
3) Sweetwater's 2 GW development remains only conditionally included in ERCOT Batch Zero; while the high-voltage substation has been energized, commercial delivery of the initial 300 MW is targeted for Q4 2027. IREN's roughly $6.0 billion FY2027 capex budget depends on external financing and customer prepayments; interim approvals do not equate to grid interconnection and revenue billing. GPU, CPU & ASIC Chip Supply & Data Center Delivery: Supply shortages continue to underpin procurement, but bottlenecks are broadening from discrete silicon to full-system data center commissioning. Industry checks indicate lead times of 25–30 weeks for server CPUs and 30–45 weeks for GPUs; AI agents are fueling demand for high-core-count data center CPUs, prompting hyperscalers to prioritize integrated, rack-scale CPU-GPU architectures. For chip vendors, customer purchase intent must be matched by available data center space, power, and liquid cooling to enable sustained delivery. When campus energization slips, orders are deferred, but inventory levels and revenue recognition bear the initial brunt. Long component lead times should not be extrapolated into synchronized upward revenue revisions across all suppliers. Nvidia: Corporate governance overhangs weighed on valuation, though near-term demand fundamentals and supply constraints have not experienced a corresponding shift.
1) Nvidia declined 3.83% on November 9, 2026. The board is investigating an undisclosed matter involving Jensen Huang; while the company confirmed he remains CEO, leadership uncertainty has increased. An internal inquiry should not be equated with an imminent executive change. Melius Research noted that acute compute shortages restrict near-term customer switching, mitigating immediate business disruption.
2) Nvidia reportedly proposed to Apollo Global Management to repurpose approximately 130 legacy Brightspeed telecom facilities into a roughly 1 GW inference network. Leveraging existing utility interconnects and fiber could compress buildout timelines, though electrical infrastructure and liquid cooling overhauls alongside local municipal permits remain prerequisites.
3) This initiative shifts the competitive battleground toward deployment velocity rather than isolated chip benchmarks. The degree of building reusability, retrofit costs per site, and deliverable power capacity will dictate whether this distributed topology becomes a viable revenue contributor. Broadcom: Hyperscaler incentives to diversify silicon sourcing have strengthened, but potential replacement opportunities should not be booked as incremental backlog.
1) Melius Research noted that Broadcom could capture incremental market share in the event of operational disruption at Nvidia, while cautioning that quantifying potential gains is premature. Acute compute shortages prevent immediate customer shifts, and substitution depends on design cycles, tape-outs, and supply-chain commitments.
2) Goldman Sachs included Broadcom in an industry tally of off-balance-sheet commitments tied to AI infrastructure, highlighting that ecosystem risks encompass downstream procurement and financing obligations alongside demand elasticity; aggregated industry figures should not be attributed directly to Broadcom's balance sheet.
3) Broadcom fell 17.21% over the trailing 20 trading sessions through November 9, 2026. For its custom ASIC business, the primary investment proof-points remain tape-out execution, production ramping, and volume delivery rather than sentiment-driven speculation stemming from competitor governance headlines. AMD: Competitive upside stems from multi-sourcing dynamics, but potential gains must be decoupled from actual procurement reallocation.
1) Melius Research identified AMD as a beneficiary poised to gain share should Nvidia experience operational disruptions, while underscoring that quantifying market share shifts remains premature. The firm expects Nvidia's near-term performance to remain robust, indicating that the substitution thesis is medium-to-long-term rather than an immediate order migration.
2) Supply-chain checks indicate hyperscalers are slated to gradually transition to next-generation platforms—including MI455—starting in Q4 2026, with an emphasis on integrated, rack-scale CPU-GPU configurations; these remain supply-chain projections subject to silicon delivery and customer acceptance.
3) Rack-scale procurement raises integration thresholds, requiring AMD to meet rigorous CPU, high-speed interconnect, and delivery benchmarks alongside raw GPU compute. AMD fell 24.43% over the trailing 20 trading sessions through November 9, 2026; broader market risk appetite should not be conflated with structural market share shifts. "Both companies could expand market share if Nvidia encounters potential operational disruption. However, the firm emphasized that it is too early to predict the actual magnitude of benefit or market share reallocation." Alchip: Rapid revenue expansion has materialized, but product mix and customer allocation dictate earnings quality.
1) Q3 revenue surged 241% quarter-over-quarter to NT$26.051 billion, driven by volume shipments of 3nm Trainium 3. Gross margin contracted to 18%, missing previous guidance of roughly 20%, due to a higher proportion of lower-margin turnkey production, wafer and substrate shortages, and deferred non-recurring engineering (NRE) revenue recognition.
2) Management guided for triple-digit percentage revenue growth in both aggregate revenue and 3nm programs for 2027. Sell-side models raised 2027 revenue estimates by 36.1% to NT$139.5 billion and EPS estimates by 45.5% to NT$220.20, while maintaining gross margin estimates at 17.9% and raising the price target to NT$6,600.
3) A second CSP anchor customer is slated to contribute volume production revenue in Q2 2027. Exclusive physical design status for 2nm Trainium 4 reinforces medium-term visibility, though advanced wafer allocation, packaging bottlenecks, and customer in-sourcing risks persist. "This growth was primarily driven by Alchip securing higher internal allocation within the customer, capturing a larger slice of a relatively fixed pie, rather than an upward revision to the customer's total program procurement." Memory & Storage (HBM / DRAM / NAND / SSD / HDD) Memory & Storage Supply-Demand Dynamics: Tight pricing and extended lead times persist across memory and storage, but monetization dynamics between DRAM, NAND, and HDDs must not be conflated. Industry data shows global Q3 DRAM revenue approached $200 billion, surging 369% year-over-year, while bit shipments grew only ~4% and average selling prices (ASPs) rose to $1.90 per gigabit, confirming that revenue expansion was almost entirely price-driven. Supply-chain checks indicate enterprise SSD lead times stand at 16 weeks and HDDs at ~50 weeks, with HDD contract pricing projected to rise through 2027. While DRAM and NAND hinge on silicon pricing cycles and mix shifts, HDDs depend on magnetic recording roadmaps and cost per terabyte. Both benefit from hyperscale buildouts, but differing competitive landscapes, capex requirements, and margin trajectories preclude a uniform investment thesis. Micron Technology: Broad-based DRAM price increases provide top-line and margin support, but customer budget elasticity and price sustainability outweigh single-quarter growth rates.
1) Q3 industry revenue growth significantly outpaced bit shipments, confirming price over volume as the primary earnings driver. Conventional DDR and LPDDR revenue grew faster than HBM, demonstrating that supply tightness extends well beyond high-bandwidth memory.
2) UBS projects that memory capex among the top 12 cloud hyperscalers will reach approximately $1.019 trillion by 2027, representing 58% of their aggregate capital expenditures; this is an industry buy-side capex forecast rather than Micron-specific order intake or revenue guidance.
3) Micron fell 30.24% over the trailing 20 trading sessions through November 9, 2026. Skepticism over AI infrastructure returns coexists with memory price inflation. Investors must evaluate whether higher ASPs can continue translating into cash generation or if customer budget constraints trigger procurement slowdowns, rather than extrapolating pricing power indefinitely. "UBS: In 2027, memory expenditures across the top 12 cloud hyperscalers will reach approximately $1.019 trillion, accounting for 58% of their total capex." Samsung Electronics: Multiple expansion depends on cycle durability rather than a single pricing wave, with legacy DRAM serving as the key litmus test.
1) BofA's Head of Korea Research suggested that Samsung and SK Hynix could command structural valuation multiples akin to TSMC if elevated margins prove sustainable; this remains sell-side analysis rather than company guidance, and memory cyclicality has not achieved foundry-like cash flow stability.
2) Q3 industry revenue growth for standard DDR and LPDDR outpaced HBM, indicating that capacity crowding from AI infrastructure has spilled into commodity memory. Evaluating Samsung requires monitoring broad-based DRAM pricing and customer absorption rather than focusing exclusively on HBM qualification.
3) Supply-chain reports indicate smartphone OEMs are recycling and re-balling legacy memory chips for budget handsets. If elevated silicon pricing forces downstream substitution or bill-of-materials destocking, demand elasticity could trigger a cyclical headwind, requiring balanced scrutiny across pricing, volumes, and downstream BOM limits. SK Hynix: Repositioning memory as critical AI infrastructure supports structural earnings visibility, but cyclical capex exposure remains an overarching risk.
1) BofA noted that procurement attitudes have shifted from treating memory as a commoditized smartphone/PC component to viewing it as permanent AI infrastructure. While this transition could stabilize procurement patterns and warrant multiple expansion, it does not imply that memory cyclicality has been eliminated.
2) Q3 industry data indicated HBM revenue nearly doubled, yet conventional DRAM growth was even faster. Robust HBM traction does not imply surplus capacity elsewhere, nor can industry-wide ASP gains be attributed solely to HBM.
3) UBS's bullish 2027 hyperscaler memory capex projections provide a constructive macro backdrop, but shipments remain tied to physical data center energization schedules. Slippage in facility buildouts could defer order recognition, with product mix and contract structures determining bottom-line sensitivity. "Buyers now view memory as long-term AI infrastructure rather than a cyclical component fluctuating with smartphone and PC upgrade cycles." SanDisk: Tight enterprise SSD availability underpins demand, but NAND market dynamics should not be conflated with DRAM pricing leverage.
1) Supply-chain checks point to ~16-week lead times for enterprise SSDs, highlighting persistent bottlenecks in hyperscale storage hardware; however, industry-wide lead times do not constitute company-specific order intake, fab allocation, or contract pricing commitments.
2) While UBS forecasts a massive expansion in 2027 hyperscaler memory spend, that total is dominated by DRAM and HBM rather than NAND, reflecting distinct budget allocations across memory tiers.
3) The stock declined 43.86% over the trailing 20 trading days and 49.12% over 60 trading days through November 9, 2026. Fundamental analysis must center on enterprise bit shipments and realized margins rather than treating the drawdown as an automatic valuation floor. If data center commissioning slips, storage procurement will follow, and extended lead times do not insulate vendors from customer scheduling revisions. Seagate Technology: Supply discipline and areal density upgrades support margin expansion, leaving market fears of price competition unsupported by operational data.
1) Morgan Stanley noted that the supply-demand deficit widened versus three months prior, with per-exabyte pricing accelerating enough to pass through component cost inflation. Capex remains tightly disciplined at 4%–6% of revenue, unit drive shipments are largely flat, and the industry's ~25% annual exabyte growth is driven primarily by areal density gains.
2) Seagate's 40TB drives are projected to account for over 50% of Heat-Assisted Magnetic Recording (HAMR) shipments by the end of Q4 2026, with HAMR representing half of nearline capacity. While higher capacity lowers TCO per terabyte, qualification cycles with tier-1 hyperscalers remain ongoing.
3) Morgan Stanley projects operating margins to expand from 36.5% in FY2026 to 67.9% in FY2028—an aggressive margin forecast. Completing customer qualifications by year-end and locking in CY2028 long-term agreements that absorb component inflation will be pivotal to hitting these targets. "As long as the industry expands capacity through technology transitions rather than adding physical manufacturing lines, the destructive price wars of past cycles are unlikely to recur." Foundry TSMC: Strict commercial procurement protocols enhance program transparency, but physical fab scheduling remains the ultimate cap on revenue velocity.
1) Alchip confirmed its role as exclusive physical design partner for Amazon's next-gen 2nm Trainium 4, noting that TSMC permits wafer orders only directly from the hyperscaler and Alchip, alleviating market concerns over unauthorized wafer capacity brokering.
2) However, direct ordering does not guarantee unrestricted fab allocation. Analysts observe that internal CSP accelerators typically rank behind commercial merchant silicon giants in the allocation queue for leading-edge nodes and advanced packaging (CoWoS); Alchip's Q3 results were constrained by wafer and substrate tightness.
3) While TSMC benefits from broadening customer diversity across custom silicon, order visibility for ASIC design partners does not guarantee delivery timing. TSMC ADRs fell 0.06% on November 9, 2026, which remains the authoritative closing benchmark. Intel: Reported technical collaboration on new fab projects carries strategic relevance, but long-dated aspirational targets cannot be modeled as contracted foundry revenue.
1) Intel is reportedly assisting Tesla and SpaceX's "Terafab" initiative to advance 2nm and 1.4nm process technology. The project has broken ground, targeting volume production in 2H 2028, but remains a development-stage engineering roadmap subject to process maturation and milestone verification.
2) The facility's aspirational target envisions 1 million wafer starts per month by 2032, comprising 700k wafers for memory and over 300k wafers for advanced logic, alongside co-located packaging and testing. This represents a long-term facility objective rather than committed foundry volume for Intel.
3) Co-developing advanced memory and leading-edge logic simultaneously imposes extraordinary process, tooling, yield, and capex hurdles. Potential upside for Intel hinges on definitive commercial terms and production milestones rather than advisory engagements being equated with captive fab expansion. Optical Interconnect & Networking Marvell Technology: Ballooning model context caches are driving multi-rack optical scale-up requirements, though the proposed acquisition expands optical capabilities while introducing execution risks.
1) Marvell stated that Key-Value (KV) cache footprints expanded roughly 10x over the past nine months. KV caches store intermediate state during model inference; surging cache sizes make confining workloads to a single rack unfeasible, expanding domain clustering from 144 XPUs to 576 XPUs and elevating the importance of optical scale-up fabrics.
2) Marvell is pursuing an all-stock acquisition of Lumentum at a fixed exchange ratio of 4.5 Marvell shares per Lumentum share, targeting a close in 1H 2028 subject to shareholder approval and multi-jurisdictional regulatory clearances.
3) Expanding cluster sizes validate the architectural thesis but do not immediately convert into recognized revenue; portfolio integration remains years away. Because equity fluctuations shift the implied transaction value, fundamental demand drivers and deal valuation dynamics must be tracked separately. Lumentum: Improving customer visibility is counterbalanced by equity deal consideration volatility; fundamental analysis cannot rely solely on transaction headlines.
1) Management highlighted improving order visibility and reiterated confidence in the strategic merits of merging with Marvell; the board elected to take 100% equity consideration after reviewing Marvell's financial health and product pipeline during due diligence.
2) The fixed exchange ratio of 4.5 Marvell shares per Lumentum share links deal value directly to Marvell's share price without downside cash collars. The stock slumped 45.89% over the trailing 20 trading sessions through November 9, 2026, reflecting both AI capex sentiment and transaction-structure beta.
3) The targeted 1H 2028 closing date remains subject to antitrust and regulatory reviews. Strong commercial demand cannot bypass regulatory scrutiny, and ultimate shareholder value will depend on standalone execution, acquirer equity performance, and post-merger integration. Ayar Labs: Optical I/O opportunities arise from cluster scaling limits, but mainstream adoption around 2028 remains an architectural projection.
1) Industry participants, including Ayar Labs, argue that copper interconnects are reaching physical reach-bandwidth limits in hyperscale clusters, positioning optical scale-up as a crucial pillar for next-generation AI infrastructure beginning around 2028.
2) While Marvell's observations regarding KV cache expansion corroborate the architectural rationale, they do not establish a commercial vendor relationship, nor do broad industry roadmaps constitute revenue guidance for Ayar Labs.
3) Achieving commercial volume requires concurrent progress across co-packaged optics design, hyperscaler qualification, and packaging yield ramps. Rising bandwidth demands incentivize adoption, but actual monetization depends on commercial system integration rather than technical white papers. Space & Satellite SpaceX: Starlink commercial deployment is accelerating, but orbital AI remains aspirational, and terrestrial compute operations face contractual and environmental constraints.
1) Lufthansa Group plans to equip approximately 850 aircraft with Starlink by year-end 2029, with Brussels Airlines operating the first commercial flight under the program; in Vietnam, 196 rural villages and civic facilities were connected.
2) SpaceX tentatively targets Q3 2027 to launch its initial Starmind satellites featuring space-optimized Vera Rubin NVL72 compute clusters; this remains an estimated timeline, and an FCC filing for up to 1 million satellites does not equate to regulatory approval or operational deployment.
3) Anthropic's $1.25 billion monthly Colossus compute contract extends through May 2029, though either party may terminate with 90 days' notice. Deutsche Bank noted that systemic compute shortages could bolster pricing power, though supply easing would compress margins; environmental permitting disputes over air emissions at the Southaven facility demonstrate that rapid infrastructure buildouts remain subject to local regulatory bottlenecks. "Deutsche Bank: If aggregate compute supply remains constrained across the industry, SpaceX could meaningfully hike prices over the coming years, boosting revenue and EBITDA while tempering capital expenditures." Rocket Lab: Focus heading into earnings centers on Neutron vehicle milestones to unlock backlog rather than isolated quarterly revenue records.
1) Consensus estimates project Q3 revenue of $257 million and an EPS loss of $0.02; these are analyst forecasts rather than reported financials. Neutron's inaugural launch schedule will dictate Rocket Lab's entry into the medium-lift market and the timing of related revenue recognition.
2) A recent $397 million U.S. Space Force contract explicitly hinges on Neutron development milestones. Further delays would defer contract cash flows and Rocket Lab's ability to deploy newly acquired satellite constellations internally, forcing continued reliance on external launch providers.
3) Space Systems operating margins represent a critical operational gauge. Satellite bus and component manufacturing must demonstrate gross margin expansion alongside volume growth to validate its vertically integrated business model; topline growth without manufacturing margin leverage will provide limited support to free cash flow. Foxconn: LEO satellite R&D is transitioning from single-satellite validation to dual-satellite constellation networking, with ground-terminal integration serving as the key to commercialization.
1) Foxconn unveiled models of its second-generation low-Earth orbit (LEO) satellites at an industry conference in Tainan, Taiwan. Two 9.5-kg test satellites, launched into ~600 km orbit on May 3, carry Ka-band inter-satellite optical/RF links, ionospheric probes, and experimental solar arrays.
2) Unlike first-generation units that evaluated basic space-to-ground links, the Gen-2 platform tests direct inter-satellite cross-links, shifting focus from isolated payloads to coordinated orbital mesh networks. Foxconn also showcased MediaTek-powered 5G terrestrial/non-terrestrial network (NTN) terminal modules, phased-array antennas, and RF front-end hardware.
3) Target applications include remote connectivity, backup networks, and industrial IoT. However, commercialization requires customer qualification cycles; integrating satellites, phased-array antennas, and user terminals into a cohesive ecosystem is required before generating material production revenue. Internet & Software Platforms Meta: Meta is establishing dedicated go-to-market channels for enterprise AI, shifting commercialization friction from model capabilities to enterprise data governance and control.
1) Meta reportedly established an in-house sales team targeting SMBs while partnering with global systems integrators—including Accenture, Deloitte, and IBM—to target enterprise accounts. Launched in September, the Meta Enterprise Platform offers the Muse Spark model, Muse Code, and enterprise agents to convert frontier AI into commercial software revenue.
2) Earlier attempts to embed agents directly onto third-party retailer websites were abandoned due to enterprise pushback over proprietary data access, branding control, and API integration friction; enterprise agents deployed within WhatsApp and Messenger have gained traction with customers such as Flipkart.
3) Channel architecture dictates customer acquisition velocity and implementation friction. Leveraging established messaging apps reduces integration hurdles, but enterprise software deployments require systems integration partners; early traction cannot be linearly extrapolated to offset massive capex commitments. Uber: Delivery Gross Bookings are approaching Mobility, yet profit conversion remains sluggish; new partnerships must prove accretive to earnings rather than merely inflating top-line GMV.
1) In Q3, Delivery Gross Bookings reached $28.539 billion with adjusted segment EBITDA of $1.057 billion; while bookings grew by $1.076 billion sequentially, segment profit expanded by only $2 million. In contrast, Mobility generated $29.512 billion in bookings and $2.362 billion in segment profit, representing an 8.0% take margin on bookings versus 3.7% for Delivery.
2) Expanding its partnership with McDonald's across 14 markets—including loyalty program integration—widens top-of-funnel customer capture. Delivery take rates ticked up from 19.1% to 19.2%, signaling improved monetization, though bottom-line conversion still demands overhead efficiency.
3) A newly introduced parking reservation feature is rolling out across 15 U.S. cities. Uber has already secured staging and parking assets for autonomous vehicle (AV) pilot partners to trim deadhead miles and cost-per-mile; optimizing physical depot logistics improves operations, but does not mean AV operations have attained commercial profitability. CrowdStrike: Strategic pricing concessions aim to drive multi-module adoption, making AI security cross-selling critical to offsetting core software discounts.
1) CrowdStrike's Falcon Flex subscription offers standard discounts of 25%–35%. Analysts estimate that transitioning existing three-year contracts creates an ARR headwind approaching $500 million, diluting roughly $750 million in gross expansion opportunity. Lower module pricing narrows the gap with competitors, but near-term ARR growth depends on cross-sell expansion rather than new logo velocity alone.
2) Wall Street models project over 80% of customers will adopt agentic security over the next three years, with the Guardian module priced at roughly 1:1 parity with legacy endpoint protection, contributing over $1.75 billion in incremental ARR by the end of FY2029.
3) Consensus models project FY2029 total revenue of $9.822 billion; the stock is rated Market Perform with an increased price target of $177.00. European enterprise AI rollouts and Next-Gen SIEM adoption represent key indicators for whether discounted bundles successfully accelerate multi-module expansion. "These proactive price cuts lower endpoint adoption barriers and bring premium pricing closer to competitor levels, encouraging clients to redirect budget savings into new security modules." IBM: Consulting partnerships for enterprise AI deployment highlight systems integration opportunities, but prospective channel roles do not equate to signed enterprise contracts.
1) Meta reportedly plans to partner with IT consultancies, including IBM, to distribute and deploy enterprise AI solutions to large corporations. Enterprise clients must resolve data privacy, governance, and architectural integration challenges; systems integrators serve to embed models into legacy enterprise workflows rather than simply reselling API access.
2) Meta's previous deployment setbacks on e-commerce sites demonstrate that enterprise procurement evaluates data governance and liability boundaries alongside raw model benchmark performance. If formalized, implementation and managed services could generate consulting revenue, though monetization depends on end-client adoption.
3) IBM gained 7.89% over the trailing 20 trading sessions through November 9, 2026, defying weakness across broader AI software peers; this relative outperformance cannot substitute for verified contract backlog, nor should contemplated partnership fees be recognized prematurely. Consumer Electronics & Electric Vehicles Apple: Robotics research demonstrates improved cross-environment generalization, but commercialization faces steep price and reliability hurdles.
1) Morgan Stanley highlighted that Apple generated multimodal synthetic data across 1,000 simulated households, achieving a 91% zero-shot task success rate across six unlabeled physical environments without fine-tuning. While this validates simulation-based pre-training to reduce manual tuning, it does not confirm commercial-grade reliability in real-world living environments.
2) Institutional surveys reveal that 72% of prospective robotics buyers require unit hardware pricing below RMB 100,000 (roughly $14,000) for commercial viability, while only 18% are satisfied with existing performance, pushing broad adoption timelines back by roughly one year. Academic research must still translate into low-latency, durable, and cost-effective physical hardware.
3) Separately, reports indicate Apple routed up to $50 billion in profits through Singapore during 2026, generating $2.7 billion in tax savings. While corporate tax optimization bolsters net income and cash flow, it cannot substitute for underlying consumer hardware demand. Tesla: Factory floor resources are shifting toward Cybercab, with the sunsetting of underperforming models occurring alongside volume growth in core vehicle lines.
1) Tesla plans to phase out Cybertruck production in roughly eight months, adding shifts to work through remaining order backlogs while refunding deposits to select reservation holders. Cybertruck annualized volume has hovered at ~28,000–32,000 units, well below the original 250,000-unit target; reallocating floor space reflects manufacturing opportunity cost.
2) Global September registrations reached 232,000 vehicles, up 9% year-over-year, led by Model Y at 165,000 units (+17% YoY). Cumulative global production crossed 10 million vehicles; baseline volume expansion across core platforms must be distinguished from the phase-out of niche models.
3) In-cabin millimeter-wave radar can detect occupants, adjust airbag deployment, and alert drivers to unattended children or pets. Management also discussed conceptual laser-cleaning systems for Robotaxi camera lenses; the latter remains an early-stage engineering concept rather than a production feature, and should not be modeled into autonomous fleet operating cost reductions. 🚨 Quelle journée de psychopathe sur Wall Street

Je vais essayer de la résumer

Le rebond sur les semis est énorme aujourd'hui. Après le krach de jeudi, le $SOXX prend +7,5 %, le Nasdaq 100 +3,5 % et le S&P 500 +2,4 %. Le VIX perd plus de 22 % et repasse sous 20

On est très loin du carnage de la semaine dernière

1. Une des PIRES journées pour Nvidia

Tout le secteur monte, sauf Nvidia. Le titre finit à -4,2 % après être descendu jusqu'à -8,8 % dans la séance, seul Mag7 dans le rouge. Bon, la journée a tournée autour de memes (hilarants) et théorie fumante, finalement peu de concret, donc essayons de trier tout cela :

A/ Côté faits : Jensen reconnaît une liaison, le board ouvre une enquête indépendante et il reste CEO. Selon le NYT, une enquête du Commerce sur Megaspeed aurait été stoppée après une intervention du juriste de Nvidia, avant d'être transférée au DOJ en pénal. 

B/ Côté allégations : le lien avec une espionne chinoise présumée, démenti par Megaspeed et par Pékin. Pour la Street, le vrai risque n'est pas un départ de Jensen, c'est Washington et les export controls en asie du sud-est.

2. Les gagnants et les perdants de l'affaire Huang vs Huang

Le marché ne vend pas la stack IA, il vend Nvidia et achète tout le reste. $AMD prend +13,4 % , $AMAT +11,4 %, $MRVL +9 %, $AVGO +8,9 %, $MU et $ASML +6,3 %. 

Même les néoclouds, rouges en pré-market qu'on disait trop lié à $NVDA, finissent dans le vert : $NBIS +9,5 % et $CRWV +5,3 %. L'idée est simple, les fonds veulent rester exposés au compute IA sans porter le risque key-man de Nvidia. BofA reste à Buy sur Nvidia avec un objectif de 350 $, mais parle d'un nouvel overhang et d'une rotation possible vers AMD, Broadcom et Marvell

3. L'IPO d'Anthropic pour cette semaine

Le roadshow peut démarrer dès demain.Le prix serait fixé au plus tôt vendredi 13 (la SEC est fermée mercredi pour Veterans Day), pour une cotation visée la semaine du 16, sous le ticker $ANT. La presse évoque une valorisation entre 1 250 et 1 750 Md$ et une levée de 75 à 100 Md$, de quoi viser ou dépasser SpaceX. Dans le S-1 : 16,96 Md$ de chiffre d'affaires au T3 (+1 127 % sur un an), une perte opérationnelle de 567 M$ et environ 132 Md$ de cash. Le chiffre que tout le monde attend, c'est l'ARR d'octobre : plus de 80 Md$ selon le WSJ, non confirmé. Et Anthropic a sorti aujourd'hui Fable 5.2 et Mythos 5.2, 30 % plus rapides et 20 % moins chers, l'écart se creuse avec OpenAI

4. Faut-il acheter l'IPO ?

Honnêtement, je n'en ai aucune idée, et je n'ai pas d'avis sur le prix d'entrée. J'ai l'impression que l'ensemble de la street est plutôt sceptique, avec une valorisation jugée trop haute après le krach. Mais historiquement, on s'était tous trompés sur SpaceX. Donc ne suivez pas les conseils financiers des gens sur une IPO de cette taille, moi compris, le consensus sans prendre de risque c'est dire que c'est sur-évalué, puis bon si on a tort, les gens nous ressortirons jamais le message... 

5. Le pétrole à la cave

Le WTI perd 4,2 % autour de 87 $ et le Brent 5,6 % autour de 93 $, au plus bas depuis dix semaines selon le FT. Trump a dit dimanche qu'il était « highly unlikely » de reprendre les frappes sur l'Iran. Moins de risque géopolitique sur l'énergie, c'est un peu d'air pour les multiples et un vent arrière pour le risk-on, les equities réagissent extrêmement bien

6. Google sort son TPU

Google a présenté aujourd'hui deux nouveaux systèmes TPU de huitième génération. Le TPU 8tx vise l'inférence confidentielle pour les gouvernements et les secteurs régulés, avec des CPU AMD EPYC en hôte. Le TPU 8i Max assemble deux puces 8i dans un seul package : deux fois plus de calcul, de SRAM et de bande passante HBM, pour les très longs contextes. Quatre systèmes TPU en un an, une première. Déploiement attendu en 2027. Encore un signal que les hyperscalers montent en puissance sur leurs puces maison face à Nvidia, et une bonne nouvelle au passage pour AMD et Broadcom. Certains analystes sont quand même confiants sur la domination de $NVDA sur Vera Rubin

AIトレンドニュース要点（CTEE記事）
詳細は該当するCTEE抽出記事Noを参照のこと

本ポストでは強調部の太字を割愛。

I. NVIDIAの調査・対中出荷とGPU／ASIC競争

NVIDIAは、CEOが外国の情報活動の標的になったとの報道を受け、独立調査を開始した。 独立取締役で構成する委員会が外部弁護士の協力を得て調査を監督し、会社はジェンスン・フアンCEOの続投方針を示した。取締役会は、現時点で米国の安全保障や会社の機密が損なわれたと考える理由はないとしている。共和党所属の米下院委員長3人は11月18日の非公開説明を求めた。Megaspeedを巡る輸出規制回避疑惑の実態、機密流出の有無、CEOの最終的な進退は不確か。11月17日予定の決算に向け、8～10月期の会社売上高見通しは1,080億米ドル±2％、市場予想は1,088.2億米ドル。CTEEは、メモリー費用の上昇を当四半期の粗利益率見通し71～72％の圧迫要因に挙げた。（記事11・12・13）

台湾の業界筋は既存受注と生産能力に変更はないと説明している。 一方、CTEEは中国の輸入承認待ちでH200約60万個が香港に滞留し、一部アジア顧客のAIサーバー注文に再確認が必要になると報じた。記事が引用するロイター報道では、中国は学習用途でH200の限定購入を認め、推論では国産チップの使用を優先する。10月末の中国の非公式市場では、H200を8基搭載したサーバーが600万元超と1年前の約3倍、Blackwell搭載機が2,000万元超だったという。台湾組立メーカーのH200出荷比率は小さく、ODMの供給の軸はB300、GB300、順次量産出荷に入るVera Rubinに移っている。注文の再確認が納期に及ぼす影響は不確か。（記事02・13）

AMDは出荷を拡大し、Googleは第8世代TPUを用途別に広げた。 AMDではデータセンター向け需要が供給を上回り、EPYCの導入拡大、Instinct MI455Xの大量出荷、複数顧客での初期Helios稼働が進む。Googleの「TPU 8tx」はAMDのカスタムx86ホストCPUを採用し、ハードウェアによる暗号化・隔離に対応する。「TPU 8i Max」は8iを2個集積し、8i比で演算性能、SRAM容量、HBM帯域を各2倍にした。GoogleはTorchTPUを公開し、PyTorchのコードやHugging Faceのモデル、推論基盤のvLLMとSGLangへの対応も進める。第10世代TPUでのAMDとの共同開発は不確か。CTEEは、NVIDIAが発注を減らせばTSMCや日月光に影響し、空いた生産枠をAMDやBroadcom、MediaTekなどが確保する可能性を挙げた。実際の発注抑制と再配分は不確か。（記事13・45）

台湾勢では、MediaTekがGoogleのTPU v8・v9関連を狙い、UBSは同社のGoogle向けTPUシェア拡大を見込む。CTEEによると、MediaTekはAIアクセラレーターで2社目の顧客を確保した。初のアクセラレーターに関する2027年の目標額は約160億米ドルとされるが、金額の指標を特定できるデータはない。創意電子はGoogleのAxion CPUを支援し、証券会社はCPU需要見通しの上方修正やCPOへの取り組みに注目する。世芯（Alchip）は米系大手2社目のASIC案件を得ており、新規顧客の売上寄与は2027年に見込まれる。中国では、アリババ傘下の平頭哥が自社AIチップ「真武V900」の2027年1～3月期の量産・販売を計画していると報じられた。（記事07・13・45・50・120）

II. 先端製造・パッケージング・検査

2nmの需要拡大が見込まれる一方、8インチの成熟工程では装置能力に制約が出ている。 UBSはTSMCの2nm需要を2028年に月約32万枚と推計し、先端ファウンドリーで80％超のシェア維持を見込む。世界先進（本文表記の銘柄コード5347）はAIサーバーやスマートフォン向けの8インチ需要が続き、一部工程で装置能力が出荷を制約していると説明した。10月売上高は47.11億台湾ドルで前年比20.53％増、前月比20.20％減。10～12月期の平均販売価格は前期比3～5％増を見込む。NXPとの合弁によるシンガポール12インチ工場VSMCは、40～130nmで電源管理、アナログ、混載信号、シリコンインターポーザーなどを対象とし、2027年1～3月期に量産を予定する。（記事07・89）

後工程では、高消費電力チップに対応する試験機改造と、パッケージング・試験の一体化が進む。 UBSは次世代のクラウド・エッジAI向け先端パッケージングの主な受益企業に日月光投控（ASE）を挙げた。JPモルガンは同社の7～9月期の粗利益率を支えた要因として、LEAPの売上構成比上昇と採算改善、従来型パッケージの値上げを挙げる。漢測は既設のウェハプローバー向け熱管理改造やプローブ清掃材を展開し、10月売上高は前年比61.88％増。同欣電は光通信・パワー半導体・高周波向けのパッケージングと試験を一体化するため、シンガポールのGTC全株式を約23.5億台湾ドルで取得する計画で、株主・関係当局などの承認を要する。緯致のICレイアウト・検証を含む半導体事業は12四半期連続で成長し、同社は年末までに約100人のレイアウト体制を計画する。（記事07・60・93・108）

3D異種集積とパネルレベル実装では、台湾電子製造設備公会の会合で、ガラス貫通孔（TGV）、精密レーザー加工、ウェハ・パネルの反りや総厚さのばらつきの計測、放熱が量産課題に挙がった。大銀微系統はナノ精度の位置制御をCoWoSやシリコンフォトニクスに展開している。長庚大学を中心とする台日共同チームは、2インチウェハ上に、ホウ素・炭素・窒素からなる厚さ約0.5nmのp型単層半導体（BCN）を形成した。n型材料との相補動作や3D集積は今後の応用候補に挙げられている。（記事79・112・145）

工場新設・増強の需要は、クリーンルーム、配管、ろ過設備に波及している。 聖暉の施工中案件は過去最高の840億台湾ドルに達した。宏璟は桃園・中壢第2園区の工場・事務所棟を日月光集団に売却した。大甲では半導体・ハイテク工場向けが売上高の約6割を占め、受注済み案件の日程は2027年、顧客需要の見通しは2028年に及ぶ。旭然は半導体・メモリー工場向け液体ろ過設備の出荷が伸び、10月売上高は8,870万台湾ドル、前年比15％増。上品は高純度薬液の貯蔵・輸送機器、達欣工は半導体工場の建設に実績を持つ。巧新は半導体装置部品を少量出荷し、精密加工などの工程で顧客検証を進める。半導体工場向けの高純度ガス配管では、強新の受注見通しに市場関係者が着目した。（記事97・110・190・230・256・258・300）

工程材料では、台塑化と台塑が原子層堆積用のルテニウム前駆体を開発する。台化・中華化などと進める電子級硫酸の生産は、第1期を2028年12月、第2期を2029年12月に予定する。南寶は半導体パッケージ用接着剤と折り畳み画面用の光学透明接着剤の少量出荷を始めた。（記事72・287）

III. HBM・DDR5への供給配分と企業向けSSD

HBMとサーバー向けDDR5の供給優先が、消費機器の価格に波及している。 台湾のIC設計会社・致新は、メモリー大手3社が両製品を優先するため、消費機器向けの供給改善が遅れ、ノートPC、スマートフォン、電子ペーパーの値上げにつながっていると説明した。致新はウェハの追加割当を求め、敦泰は一部の受託生産枠がAI向けに回るなかで安全在庫を積み増した。広達はメモリー不足と最終製品の値上がりを背景に、通年のノートPC出荷を二桁減と予想する。新日興のノートPC用ヒンジも部材高と流通在庫の影響を受けた。一方、宏碁の10月PC売上高は前年比17.8％増で、CTEEはPCの平均販売価格上昇が台湾ブランド各社の売上を支えたと伝えた。（記事15・59・90・109）

企業向けSSDは需要が底堅く、部材を確保しても顧客検証が遅れれば採算に影響する。 群聯（Phison）の7～9月期AI関連売上高は前期比88％増、全体の約57％となった。同社は2027年の旧正月後に企業向けSSDの供給が逼迫する可能性を指摘する。宜鼎ではAI関連売上構成が4割を超えた一方、代替フラッシュ部品の顧客検証が遅れ、滞留在庫の損失が粗利益率を約6ポイント押し下げたと証券会社は推計する。威剛は2027年を通じたDRAM不足の可能性を指摘し、十銓は2026年10～12月期から2027年4～6月期末までが最も厳しいとみる。添付にはHBMの世代別価格・供給量のデータがない。（記事81・90）

供給体制では、SK hynixがNVIDIAなどとの連携を深めるため、米国のチップ事業部門の再編と人員拡充を計画している。テスラとSpaceXが進めるTerafabは、報道によれば2032年にウェハ月産100万枚、うちメモリー70万枚、ロジック30万枚を目標とする。Intelの技術支援を受け、ロジックでは14Aの採用を検討し、TSMCと協議を再開したとも報じられた。TSMCとの協業成立と生産目標の達成は不確か。（記事43・147）

IV. AIサーバーの出荷・受注とデータセンター投資

10月のサーバー出荷が台湾各社の売上に表れた。 広達（Quanta）は3,532.5億台湾ドルで前年比104％増、仁宝（Compal）は871.51億台湾ドルで40.7％増。ASUSは繰り越し分を含む納入でグループ売上高が1,076.2億台湾ドル、62.25％増となった。広達は通年のAIサーバー三桁成長、汎用サーバー二桁成長の目標を維持した。緯穎（Wiwynn）の7～9月期純利益は過去最高の233.64億台湾ドル。外資系証券は、汎用サーバー、AI ASIC、AMD GPUの出荷を背景に、同社の10～12月期売上高が前期比20％増と予想する。（記事15・59・121）

サーバー受注規模が維持される中で、部材不足がラックの出荷時期を左右し得る。 信驊をカバーする外資系証券5社は、汎用・AIサーバー需要への前向きな見方を維持しつつ目標株価を引き下げた。JPモルガンの調査ではサーバー受注規模は維持されており、同社はメモリーなどの部材調達とラック出荷にずれが生じるリスクを挙げた。UBSによると、信驊は2027年まで注文が見通せる状況で、次世代サーバー遠隔管理チップ（BMC）「AST2700」に比較的調達しやすいEガラスのBT基板を採用し、パッケージング・試験大手2社と契約した。佳世達はAIサーバーと1.6Tスイッチを受注し、年末までの少量出荷、2027年4～6月期からのAIサーバー本格出荷を見込む。宏碁傘下の安圖斯はGPUをプール化して割り当てる「Altos BrainSphere R880 F8」を発表し、同社の1～10月売上高は前年比57.3％増だった。（記事10・61・197）

台湾では、高雄のGB300採用計算拠点が第一金私募股権の投資対象に挙がり、訓練・推論・クラウド計算向けの建設・運営が計画されている。大大寬頻も法人回線に加え、AI計算・クラウドデータセンターを計画する。彭啓明環境部長は、米国で問題視される低周波騒音や電力・水の消費を挙げ、台湾でもデータセンターの環境・技術基準の検討を始めたと述べた。台湾経済部は別の大気汚染防止法改正案について、西部のハイテク工場や発電所の許可更新が頻繁になると懸念している。（記事33・238・288・289）

米国では中間選挙後の建設制約を巡り、立地、進捗、インフラ費用の負担先が変わり得るとの見方が出た。米メディアによれば、Metaが開発案件で地方政府に秘密保持契約を求めたことも議会調査の焦点になり得る。台湾の運用会社は、Metaなどが本業利益で設備投資を賄えるか、債務負担が増すかを信用面の論点に挙げる。通信事業会社のソフトバンクは、米国で需要が減速した場合に他国での事業先行を検討し、世界全体の需要は強いとの見方を示した。建設の遅れが実際の発注取り消しに及ぶかは不確か。（記事40・54・88・129・135・177）

V. CCL・ABF／BT基板と多層PCB

1.6TスイッチがABF基板を、メモリー需要がBT基板を押し上げている。 南亞の10月電子材料売上高は前年比104.7％増で、全体の61.5％を占めた。高級CCLは出荷と認証が並行し、証券会社は値上げ傾向の継続を見込む。南亞電路板では、法人の見立てで7～9月期にABF・BT基板の価格がともに10％超上昇した。米系顧客のサーバーCPU向けは2027年1～3月期から出荷拡大を見込む。国泰の調査部門は、大型・多層化で材料使用量と必要な生産能力が増え、2027年のABF基板は供給不足になると予測する。國精化も高速演算向けの高級CCL用化学材料を開発している。Tガラスの単価・出荷量はデータがない。（記事104・110・119）

多層化に対応する生産能力をタイなどで増やしている。 定穎はタイで20層以上のAIサーバー用基板を量産し、12月に少量出荷する予定。30層品と40層以上品は10～12月期に順次量産し、2027年1～3月期末の出荷開始を見込む。中国工場はフル稼働、タイは約70％で、タイの関連生産枠は主要顧客が確保したという。黄石とタイへの追加投資はそれぞれ99.2億、80億台湾ドルで、2027年7～9月期、10～12月期に能力が加わる見込み。騰輝電子は400V・800VのAIサーバー電源用材料を10～12月期に量産予定で、昆山では15億台湾ドルを投じてデータセンター向け高級材料の設備を改装し、2027年4～6月期の量産を計画する。同社のタイ新工場は少量出荷に入り、年末に量産予定。華通の10月売上高はデータセンター製品の増量出荷などで前年比24.74％増、國巨はAI需要と汎用品・特殊品の成長で55％増となった。國巨は10～12月期の稼働率を両品種とも95％超、受注出荷比率を2超と見込む。（記事66・91・92・95）

原材料では、台湾の運用会社がデータセンター、電力網、電化による金属需要増を指摘した。貝萊德投信の担当者は、データセンターの電力容量が2025年の82GWから2030年に219GWへ増えると推計する。LMEの銅3カ月物は11月9日の取引時間中に1トン当たり13,859.5米ドルとなった。記事では供給逼迫が価格を支え、米国のAI設備建設への規制が需要側の懸念とされた。（記事131・246・281）

VI. 電力・液冷・ラック部材と高速光通信

高出力電源は出荷が始まり、高電圧のラック電源は製品ごとに検証・導入段階が異なる。 台達電の10月売上高は746.66億台湾ドル、前年比30.12％増。Vera Rubin向け18.3kW電源を出荷し、±400VDC品は少量出荷に入った。光寶科は200.71億台湾ドル、32.01％増で、18.3kW電源、110kW電源システム、バッテリー・バックアップ（BBU）の出荷が伸びた。800VDC電源ラックはサンプル検証中で、2027年1～3月期からASIC顧客を中心に出荷を予定する。台達電はCOP31で蓄電、水素、高効率電力変換を組み合わせたマイクログリッドを紹介する予定で、固体酸化物形燃料電池（SOFC）は2027年の出荷を計画する。台達電基金会は2030年の世界のAI向け電力消費を9,450億kWh、水使用量を93億立方メートルと見積もる。添付の短報は、Bloom EnergyとNTT DATAがデータセンター向け燃料電池900MWの導入で合意したと伝えている。（記事14・16・163）

部材需要は計算ラックから電源・CPU用の周辺ラックにも広がる。 証券会社は、Vera Rubinで周辺ラックの導入が進めば、川湖（King Slide）の高級レールの数量と単価が上がるとみる。南俊國際では、顧客が中国・台湾以外での生産を求めるなか、ベトナム工場のEagle Stream向けレールの生産枠が埋まった。経宝精密（jpp-KY）は電源・BBU・蓄電向け機構部品を供給し、電源と無停電管理用の機構部品が10～12月期に本格量産に入った。貝爾威勒電子は高級コネクター・ハーネスの需要増が製品構成の改善につながり、7～9月期の粗利益率は56％だった。液冷では、智伸科が水冷モジュール部品を展開し、時碩はサーバー冷却部品の増量などで10月売上高が前年比61.7％増、大甲は高耐圧・耐食性の配管を開拓する。（記事78・98・121・256・262・269・272・291）

800Gスイッチは出荷が伸び、1.6Tは順次量産・納入に進む。 智邦は800Gスイッチの出荷が堅調で、1.6T品が順次量産に入った。佳世達は北米向け1.6Tスイッチを年末までに順次出荷し、3.2Tも開発する。同社は800G・1.6Tのシリコンフォトニクス光トランシーバーの売上寄与を2027年10～12月期に見込む。GIS-KYは高速光通信用の300～400mW級以上の連続波レーザーを対象に、11～12月のパッケージ量産開始を予定する。生産能力が揃うのは2027年4～6月期末から7～9月期の見通し。投資額40～50億台湾ドルの約3分の1を台湾、残りをベトナムに振り向け、光ファイバーアレイ用部品も開発する。汎銓のシリコンフォトニクス計測機器「MSS HG」の実機評価には顧客25組が参加し、富采はAI光通信で協力する友達の株式を子会社経由で15億台湾ドル買い増した。（記事61・64・96・107・252）

VII. 台湾の輸出・地域分散と株式市場

10月の台湾輸出は967.6億米ドルで過去最高、前年比58.9％増だった。 情報通信・視聴覚製品は476億米ドルで72.9％増、電子部品は326.8億米ドルで61.4％増。サーバーとグラフィックスカードは過去最高で、ストレージ、スイッチ、ルーターも倍増規模だった。対米輸出は329.3億米ドル。メモリー需要増と価格上昇を背景に、韓国がシェア18.9％で台湾最大の輸入元となった。台驊の空運売上高はAI・半導体・電子部品の輸送が寄与して43.88％増え、同社は米国向けを中心にサービスを広げている。台湾経済研究院はCSPと主権AIの投資が半導体・先端実装・サーバー需要を支えると予測する。確定済みの注文や建設許可が2027年上期の支えになるとし、下期の伸びは不確かとみる。（記事03・17・263・278）

台湾・マレーシアの通商協議は棚上げになったと報じられた。日月光、頎邦、矽品が現地で増設してきたなか、業界筋は新規半導体投資に影響する可能性を指摘する。米国は一部PCB・光電設備などを含む中国製品178品目の追加関税除外を2027年1月9日まで延長。中国は米国16実体向け輸出管理などの停止を2カ月延長した。対象実体へのデュアルユース品輸出には申請と審査が必要とされる。（記事20・47・292）

株式市場では、出荷の伸びとAI投資の回収・規制への懸念が併存した。 シティは米国株全体と世界・欧州のテクノロジー株の判断を中立に引き下げた。ゴールドマンの集計では、前週のヘッジファンドによる世界のテクノロジー株の売却ペースが2016年以来で最も速かった。米テクノロジー株の下落にはヘッジ調整やレバレッジ解消も重なったとの見方がある。台湾株は9日に1,960ポイント高の41,661で引け、公的銀行系と投信の買いはTSMC、創意電子、欣興などに入った。海外投資家は現物を900.56億台湾ドル売り越し、先物のネットショートは10万1,771枚。前週の海外投資家の売り越しは156.99億米ドルで、6週連続だった。光学関連では大立光、先進光、今國光に反発が広がる一方、景碩、ガラスクロスの富喬、光通信の聯亞の株式取引では決済不履行が報告された。（記事04・08・83・87・117・130・173・191・209）

VIII. エッジAI・産業機器・衛星通信

融程電は無人機・ロボット向けの堅牢型エッジAI機器を展開し、和暢科技はMediaTek、NXP、Rockchipの認定設計パートナーとして組み込み機器を開発する。泓格科技はセンサーとエッジ処理による製造設備の予知保全を紹介する予定。遠傳と淡江大学はMicrosoft Azure上で電力管理と3Dデジタルツインの運用を始め、AI分析を今後の用途に位置づける。精密部品では鈞興が、1～10月に売上が最も伸びた品目はロボット用歯車だったと説明した。（記事85・98・114・142・264）

台湾の第3期宇宙計画は予算が710億台湾ドルに増え、期間が2031年まで延びた。鴻海、緯創、仁宝などが参加した宇宙産業展では、電子・通信部材から衛星システム統合への展開が議論された。台湾当局の衛星会合では、日台の非地上系ネットワークの実証協力、日英との海事・防災分野での連携、衛星データとAI・クラウドを組み合わせる用途が取り上げられた。事欣科は衛星用通信モジュールの試作受注を得て、10～12月期に正式出荷の見込み。鐳洋科技はKa帯アクティブアレイアンテナとKu帯地上機器を展示し、「黒鳶」の2機が軌道上で稼働、後続2機が統合試験に入った。（記事24・86・221・260・270）

まとめ｜AIトレンドの核心

台湾の足元を支えるのはサーバーと電子部品の実出荷。 
10月は輸出とODM売上が伸びた。NVIDIAの調査や対中審査が納期・将来の受注に及ぼす影響は不確かで、11月17日予定の決算と、米下院委員長らが18日の開催を求めた非公開説明が焦点となる。
（記事02・03・11・12・15・263）

クラウドの計算基盤はGPUと専用ASICの両方で広がっている。 
AMDはMI455Xを出荷し、顧客で初期Heliosが稼働した。Googleは機密処理とメモリー帯域を重視したTPUを追加し、台湾のIC設計会社も新規顧客を確保した。NVIDIAからの生産枠の再配分は不確か。
（記事13・45・120）

機器を発注してから稼働させるまでの供給条件に差がある。 
HBM・サーバーDDR5の優先配分は消費機器に波及し、AI向けでも多層基板、1.6T、高電圧給電、レーザーパッケージングの量産・納入時期が異なる。
（記事14・61・90・91・96・107・119）

建設のペースと投資回収が次の焦点。 
台湾・米国で環境、電力、水、立地、費用負担が論点となり、株式・信用市場ではAI投資を本業の利益や資金調達でどこまで支えられるかが問われている。
（記事54・129・135・173・289）
